newsitem.title: USA: Dole, in California, stresses immigration, ethics.
newsitem.headline: Dole, in California, stresses immigration, ethics.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole hammered away at President Bill Clinton on illegal immigration and ethics on Saturday, hoping to cut his Democratic rival's commanding lead in this key state.

"I smell victory in California," Dole told a large crowd at a park in Visalia as he began a "Rally the Valley" bus tour of the agricultural Central Valley, where about 20 percent of the state's voters live.

Standing before a huge mural emblazoned with the word "Trust," Dole accused the president of not doing enough to stop illegal immigration, a major issue in the state, and said Clinton's "war on California" had hurt businesses and farmers.
He stepped up his charges later at a rally in the town of Selma.

"Suddenly now in an election year, President Clinton is moving all these (immigration) agents from other states into California trying to make it appear he's really going to get tough," Dole said. "Why did you wait four years, Mr. President?"

The Dole campaign has decided to focus much of its time and energy on this prize state in the 10 days before the election. California has 54 of the 270 Electoral College votes needed to win the White House.
But a Los Angeles Times poll earlier this week showed Dole trailing Clinton by 20 points here.
Throughout the day, Dole punched away at Clinton, making the case that his administration was too corrupt for him to be re-elected.

He reeled off a list of scandals, from questions about possible illegal donations to the Democrats from foreign interests to the Whitewater affair and the White House's improper acquisition of 900 FBI files on Republicans. "Where is the outrage, where is the outrage?" he asked over and over.
"Can you imagine a Republican president doing any of those things? No," Dole said in Visalia.

Then, apparently remembering the scandal that brought down former Republican President Richard Nixon, he added: "In fact, Watergate wasn't very pleasant for Republicans. I know somebody who went to jail for looking at one FBI file, one FBI file. Not 900."
Later, in Fresno, Dole said Republicans had been punished for Watergate and probably should have been.

The Kansas Republican, badly wounded in the Second World War, criticised Clinton in Fresno for not serving in Vietnam. "I've never said a thing about the president's record in the service -- lack of record, let's put it that way. But I am just a little unnerved when I see him wearing those army fatigues like he's been in the army all his life," he said.

The Dole campaign unveiled on Friday an immigration advertisement targeting California. To footage of prisoners and of police officers hustling someone into a squad car, an announcer complains of 20,000 illegal immigrants in prisons and two million statewide.
Immigration has been a hot issue in California, where 59 percent of voters approved a proposition to deny nearly all benefits to illegal immigrants. Its implementation has been held up in the courts.
Clinton has made a concentrated effort to woo California since taking office, visiting the state about 30 times and dispensing government defence contracts and other aid.

Republican Gov. Pete Wilson and Dole charged the White House was rushing through citizenship applications for legal immigrants without doing needed background checks, to make sure they could vote on Nov. 5, even though up to 10 percent might have criminal backgrounds.

The FBI has said 10 percent of immigrants show up on FBI files but this does not indicate that they have criminal records. There has been an upsurge in naturalisation applications, apparently in part because of new laws restricting government benefits to legal aliens.

Dole, who has lashed out at reporters in recent days, accusing them of ignoring White House ethics problems, said on Saturday he was sorry if he had offended the press corps. He then repeated some of his charges about reporting on ethics.
